gloss: one; one and the same; a certain one; first; once
summary: אֶחָד is the number one: a single thing, set against two or many (Deu 32:30; Ecc 4:8–9). From that it is one and the same, many made one (one flesh, one people, one law: Gen 2:24; 34:16; Num 15:16); a certain one, or one of several (1Sa 1:1); each, in a share-out (Num 7:11); the first in a count of days and dates (Gen 1:5; Lev 23:24); and, as feminine אַחַת, once (Exo 30:10). Its weightiest use is “Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one” (Deu 6:4), which Jesus calls the first of all the commandments. Aramaic חַד, in Daniel, Ezra and the Peshitta, is the same word without its first letter; Arabic ʾaḥad, Ugaritic aḥd, Punic ʾḥd and Geʿez ʾäḥädu all mean “one”.

words.gloss: one; one and the same; a certain one; each; first; (fem.) once
words.summary: Masculine אֶחָד, feminine אַחַת, plural אֲחָדִים, construct אַחַד: one of the commonest words in scripture (970 uses). It agrees with its noun and usually follows it (פַּר אֶחָד, “one bull”), and its uses range from plain counting to the confession of Deu 6:4.

senses.definition: The number one: a single person or thing, counted, and set against two or more.

evidence.note: Two silver trumpets are made (Num 10:2); when both are blown the whole congregation gathers (10:3), “and if they blow with one (בְּאַחַת), then the chiefs gather to you”.
With the new grain offering, “seven lambs … and one (אֶחָד) bull … and two rams”: one counted beside seven and two.
“One (אֶחָד) kid of the goats for a sin offering, and two lambs.”
“How should one (אֶחָד) chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight?”
“Two are better than the one (הָאֶחָד).”
One (אֶחָד) cluster of grapes, carried on a pole between two.
“Twelve brothers, sons of one (אֶחָד) man … and the one (הָאֶחָד) is not.”
“One (אֶחָד) man of you shall chase a thousand.”
Ten women shall bake bread in one (אֶחָד) oven.
Seven women shall take hold of one (אֶחָד) man.

senses.gloss: in one day: at a stroke
senses.definition: Of time, a single day: what happens בְּיוֹם אֶחָד happens all at once, with no time between.

evidence.note: “These two shall come to you in a moment, in one day (בְּיוֹם אֶחָד): loss of children and widowhood.”
“Shall a land be brought forth in one day (בְּיוֹם אֶחָד)? Shall a nation be born at once (פַּעַם אֶחָת)?”
“Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”
Yahweh cuts off head and tail, palm branch and rush, in one day.
“I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.”

senses.definition: Joined to ten and the tens, as אַחַד עָשָׂר “eleven” and the like.

evidence.note: Jacob takes “his eleven (אַחַד עָשָׂר) children” over the Jabbok.
“Eleven (אַחַד עָשָׂר) days from Horeb by the way of mount Seir.”

senses.definition: One and no more: a single person or thing with no second beside it, and so unique, beyond compare.

evidence.note: “There is one (אֶחָד), and there is no second; he has neither son nor brother.”
Esau: “Have you only one (אַחַת) blessing, my father? Bless me, me also.”
“Look to Abraham your father … for I called him one (אֶחָד), and blessed him and multiplied him”: one alone, made many.
“Abraham was one (אֶחָד), and he inherited the land; but we are many.”
“My dove, my undefiled, is one (אַחַת); she is the only one (אַחַת) of her mother, the choice one (בָּרָה) of her that bore her”: unique among the many queens of 6:8.
“What one (אֶחָד) nation in the earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem?”
“But he is in one (בְאֶחָד), and who can turn him? What his soul desires, he does”: of one mind, alone and unswayed.

senses.definition: With a negative, not even one: none at all.

evidence.note: “They have all turned aside, together they have become corrupt; there is none who does good, not even one (אֵין גַּם־אֶחָד).” Paul quotes it in Rom 3:12.
“Of the cattle of the sons of Israel not one (לֹא־מֵת אֶחָד) died.”
“Not even one (עַד־אֶחָד) of the cattle of Israel had died.”
“Not one (אֶחָד) locust remained in all the border of Egypt.”
“There is none that does good, there is not so much as one (ἕως ἑνός)”, quoting Psa 14:3.

senses.gloss: one and the same; made one, united
senses.definition: Many things or people that are one: the same in kind, sharing one speech, law, heart or purpose, or joined together into a single whole. The text names the parts that are made one.

evidence.note: A man “shall cleave to his wife, and they shall become one (אֶחָד) flesh”: two made one.
The curtains are coupled one to another with the clasps, “and the tabernacle shall be one (אֶחָד)”.
“Join them one (אֶחָד) to another (אֶחָד) into one (אֶחָד) stick, and they shall become one (לַאֲחָדִים) in your hand.”
“I will make them one (אֶחָד) nation in the land … and one (אֶחָד) king shall be king to them all, and they shall no more be two nations.”
“All the earth was of one (אֶחָת) language and of the same (אֲחָדִים) words.”
“Behold, one (אֶחָד) people, and one (אַחַת) language for them all.”
Two dreams, but “the dream of Pharaoh is one (אֶחָד)”: one meaning.
“We will dwell with you and become one (אֶחָד) people.”
“One (אַחַת) law shall be for the native and for the stranger.”
“One (אַחַת) law and one (אֶחָד) ordinance shall be for you and for the stranger.”
“All the people answered with one (אֶחָד) voice.”
“I will give them one (אֶחָד) heart and one (אֶחָד) way, to fear me all the days.”
“I will give them one (אֶחָד) heart, and I will put a new spirit within you.”
The peoples will call on the name of Yahweh “to serve him with one (אֶחָד) shoulder”.
The congregation gathered “as one (אֶחָד) man”.
“One (אֶחָד) event befalls them … they have all one (אֶחָד) breath, and man has no advantage over the beast.”
“All go to one (אֶחָד) place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust.”
“Did he not make one (אֶחָד)? … And why one (הָאֶחָד)? He sought a godly seed”: of marriage, with Gen 2:24 behind it; the verse’s syntax is hard.
The words of the wise “are given from one (אֶחָד) shepherd”.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: one, with no other God beside him; the one God and Father who made all.

evidence.note: “Hear, O Israel: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one (אֶחָד).” Moses has just said “Yahweh, he is God; there is none else beside him” (Deu 4:35, 39).
Jesus quotes Deu 6:4–5 as the first of all the commandments; the scribe expounds it, “he is one, and there is none other but he” (Mrk 12:32), and Jesus says he answered discreetly (12:34).
“Yahweh shall be king over all the earth; in that day Yahweh shall be one (אֶחָד) and his name one (אֶחָד).”
“Have we not all one (אֶחָד) father? Has not one (אֶחָד) God created us?”
“Did not he who made me in the womb make him, and did not one (אֶחָד) fashion us in the womb?”
“To us there is one (εἷς) God, the Father, of whom are all things … and one Lord Jesus Christ.”

senses.definition: One not yet named, “a certain …”; with מִן or a following noun, one out of a number.

evidence.note: “There was a certain (אֶחָד) man of Ramathaim-zophim … and his name was Elkanah.”
“There was a certain (אֶחָד) man of Zorah … whose name was Manoah.”
Elisha called “one (לְאַחַד) of the sons of the prophets”.
“Behold, the man has become as one (כְּאַחַד) of us, to know good and evil.”
“Offer him there for a burnt offering on one (אַחַד) of the mountains that I will tell you.”
Hagar cast the child under one (אַחַד) of the shrubs.
“Out of one (הָאַחַת) of them came forth one (אַחַת) little horn.”

senses.definition: In a share-out, one to each: often doubled, “one … one”, for “one at a time, each”.

evidence.note: “One (אֶחָד) chief a day, one (אֶחָד) chief a day, shall they offer their offering.”
“Take twelve men from the people, one (אֶחָד) man, one (אֶחָד) man from each tribe.”
“A rod for one chief, a rod for one chief”: a rod for each, twelve rods.
“You shall be gathered one by one (לְאַחַד אֶחָד), O sons of Israel.”
“Each one (לְאַחַת) had four faces, and each one (לְאַחַת) had four wings.”

senses.definition: Paired with a second אֶחָד or with “second”: the one … the other, one … another.

evidence.note: Aaron and Hur held up Moses’ hands, “one (אֶחָד) on this side and one (אֶחָד) on that side”.
“The name of the one (הָאֶחָד) was Gershom … and the name of the other (הָאֶחָד) Eliezer” (18:4).
“The inhabitants of one (אַחַת) city shall go to another (אַחַת), saying, Let us go to entreat Yahweh.”
“And one (חַד) speaks with another (אַחַד)”: Hebrew אַחַד beside the Aramaic-looking חַד.

senses.gloss: first (in a count, and of dates)
senses.definition: The first of a series, where a count begins “one, second, third …”; above all in dates, בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ “on (day) one of the month”, the first day.

evidence.note: “There was evening and there was morning, day one (יוֹם אֶחָד)”, followed by “a second day” (1:8), “a third day” (1:13), to the sixth (1:31).
Of the four rivers, “the name of the one (הָאֶחָד) is Pishon”, then “the name of the second river” (2:13).
“In the seventh month, on the first (בְּאֶחָד) of the month, you shall have a sabbath-rest, a memorial of blowing (זִכְרוֹן תְּרוּעָה), a holy convocation.”
“In the tenth month, on the first (בְּאֶחָד) of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.”
“In the six hundred and first (בְּאַחַת) year, in the first month, on the first (בְּאֶחָד) of the month, the waters were dried up.”
“On the day of the first month, on the first (בְּאֶחָד) of the month, you shall set up the tabernacle.”
“On the first (בְּאֶחָד) of the second month, in the second year.”
“By the first (אֶחָד) day of the first month.”
“Toward the first (μίαν, ‘one’) of the week”: the New Testament keeps the Hebrew way of counting the first day as “one”.

senses.definition: The feminine אַחַת, alone or with פַּעַם “time”, is “once”: a single time, not to be repeated, or once in a stated period.

evidence.note: “Aaron shall make a covering on its horns once (אַחַת) in the year, with the blood of the sin offering of coverings; once (אַחַת) in the year he shall make a covering on it.”
“To make a covering for the sons of Israel for all their sins once (אַחַת) in the year.”
“Once (אַחַת) have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie to David”: once, and needing no repeating.
“Once (אַחַת) has God spoken; twice have I heard this.”
“For God speaks once (בְאַחַת), yes twice, though man does not perceive it.”
“Not once (אַחַת) nor twice.”
“Go around the city once (פַּעַם אֶחָת).”
“Yet once (עוֹד אַחַת), it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens and the earth”; Heb 12:26–27 expounds the “yet once”.
Of Lev 16: the high priest went in “once every year (ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ), not without blood”; the Peshitta has חְדָא בְּשַׁנְתָּא, word for word the Hebrew אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה.

senses.definition: With כְּ, “as one”: all together, at one time, or all alike.

evidence.note: “The wolf and the lamb shall feed as one (כְּאֶחָד)”: together.
“The whole congregation together (כְּאֶחָד) was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty.”
“Whether both alike (כְּאֶחָד) shall be good.”
Jeshua, Kadmiel and their sons stood “as one (כְּאֶחָד)” to oversee the work.
“The priests and the Levites had purified themselves as one (כְּאֶחָד).”
“The trumpeters and singers were as one (כְאֶחָד), to make one (אֶחָד) sound to be heard in praising and thanking Yahweh.”

senses.definition: The plural, of days: “a few”, a short time, so few they are almost “one”.

evidence.note: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, “and they seemed to him but a few (אֲחָדִים) days, for the love he had for her”.
“Stay with him a few (אֲחָדִים) days, until your brother’s fury turns away.”
“Within few (אֲחָדִים) days he shall be broken.”

parallels.note: “Pure, choice”, beside אַחַת of the one beloved, unique among many.
“One father” beside “one God”: the one who made them all.

opposites.note: “Two”: one set against two, or two made one.
“Many”: Abraham was one, and Yahweh made him many.

phrases.gloss: as one man: all together, with one mind
on the first of the month
day one, the first day; one day, a single day

evidence.locator: Deu.6.4, אֶחָד → εἷς; Gen.1.5, אֶחָד → μία; Gen.2.24, אֶחָד → μίαν; Lev.23.18–19, אֶחָד → ἕνα; Psa.14.3, אֶחָד → ἑνός; εἷς renders אֶחָד ×437 and its feminine μία ×253

evidence.note: Jesus quotes Deu 6:4, κύριος εἷς ἐστιν, as the first of all the commandments.
The scribe: “there is one (εἷς) God, and there is none other but he.”
Gen 2:24 quoted: “the two shall be one (μίαν) flesh”; “so they are no more two, but one flesh” (19:6).
Psa 14:3 quoted: “not so much as one (ἑνός)”.
“One (μία) flock, one (εἷς) shepherd”, as Ezk 34:23 and 37:24 have רֹעֶה אֶחָד.
“On the first (τῇ μιᾷ) of the week”: “one” for “first”, as in Gen 1:5.

evidence.locator: Exo.30.10, אַחַת → ἅπαξ (twice); Lev.16.34; Psa.62.12; Psa.89.36; ἅπαξ renders אֶחָד ×11. Hag.2.6 עוֹד אַחַת מְעַט → ἔτι ἅπαξ, the alignment pairing ἅπαξ with מְעַט

evidence.note: The high priest entered “once (ἅπαξ) every year”, as Exo 30:10 and Lev 16:34.
Hag 2:6 quoted: “yet once (ἔτι ἅπαξ) I shake not the earth only but also heaven”; 12:27 expounds “yet once”.
“Now once (ἅπαξ) in the end of the ages he has been manifested to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.”

evidence.locator: Gen.8.5, בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ → πρῶτος; Ezr.7.9; Dan.9.1–2; πρῶτος renders אֶחָד ×10

evidence.note: “Early on the first (πρώτῃ) of the week”, where Mrk 16:2 has μιᾷ: the two words for the one day.

words.summary: The Aramaic form of אֶחָד, once in Hebrew, beside אַחַד in the same phrase. Its tokens are counted under the Aramaic word below, whose key also files this one.

senses.definition: “One with another”: Ezekiel’s people talking among themselves.

evidence.note: “And one (חַד) speaks with another (אַחַד), each man with his brother, saying, Come, hear what the word is that comes from Yahweh.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic חַד, feminine חֲדָה, in Daniel and Ezra: the same word as Hebrew אֶחָד, with the same range from “one” to “first”.

senses.definition: One in number, or “a” where a thing is first brought in; with מִן, one of several.

evidence.note: “A stone (אֶבֶן חֲדָה) was brought and laid on the mouth of the den.”
Over the satraps, three presidents, “of whom Daniel was one (חַד)”.
“Behold, a great image (צְלֵם חַד).”
“I came near to one (חַד) of those who stood by.”
The bear “raised itself up on one (חַד) side”.
Rehum and Shimshai “wrote a letter (אִגְּרָה חֲדָה) against Jerusalem”.
At Achmetha “a scroll (מְגִלָּה חֲדָה) was found”.
Daniel was astonished “for one hour (כְּשָׁעָה חֲדָה)”: for a while.

senses.definition: One for all alike.

evidence.note: “If you will not make known to me the dream, there is one (חֲדָה) decree for you”: one sentence for all the wise men.

senses.definition: In dates, “year one” of a king: his first year.

evidence.note: “In the first year (בִּשְׁנַת חֲדָה) of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree to build this house of God.”
“In the first year (בִּשְׁנַת חֲדָה) of Belshazzar king of Babylon.”

senses.definition: With כְּ, “as one”: all at the same moment.

evidence.note: “Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were broken in pieces together (כַחֲדָה)” by the stone.

senses.definition: “One seven”: seven times over.

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar commanded “to heat the furnace one seven (חַד־שִׁבְעָה) more than it was wont to be heated”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܚܕ (ḥad), feminine ܚܕܐ (ḥdā). Its New Testament says in the same word what the Hebrew says with אֶחָד: one God, one flesh, one shepherd, “not even one”, once a year, and “one in the week” for the first day.

senses.definition: The one God, set beside the one mediator, the man Jesus Christ.

evidence.note: Peshitta: מָרְיָא אַלָהַן מָרְיָא חַד הוּ, “the Lord our God is one Lord”, from Deu 6:4.
Peshitta: “he is one (דְּחַד), and there is no other besides him.”
Peshitta: “to us there is one (חַד) God, the Father … and one (וְחַד) Lord, Jesus the Messiah.”
Peshitta: “For God is one (חַד), and one (וְחַד) is the mediator of God and men, the man (בַּרְנָשָׁא) Jesus the Messiah.”
Peshitta: “but God is one (חַד).”
Peshitta: “and one (וְחַד) God, the Father of all.”

senses.definition: Two or many made one: husband and wife, the flock, the disciples with the Father and the Son.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “and the two of them shall be one (חַד) flesh; so they are not two, but one (חַד) flesh.”
Peshitta: “the whole flock shall be one (חְדָא) and one (וְחַד) shepherd.”
Peshitta: “that they may be one (חַד) as we are one (חַד).”
Peshitta: “I and my Father are one (חַד).”
Peshitta: “in one (בְּחַד) body and in one (וּבְחְדָא) spirit … in one (בְּחַד) hope.”

senses.definition: Not even one.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “there is none who does good, not even one (אָפְלָא חַד)”, quoting Psa 14:3 אֵין גַּם־אֶחָד.

senses.gloss: חַד בְּשַׁבָּא: the first day of the week
senses.definition: “One in the week”: the first day, counted as Gen 1:5 counts “day one”.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “at the dawning of one in the week (חַד בְּשַׁבָּא)”.

senses.definition: One time: once a year, or “yet once”.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “once (חְדָא הוּ) in the year the high priest went in”, as Hebrew אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה.
Peshitta: “yet once more (תּוּב חְדָא זְבַן) I shake”, from Hag 2:6 עוֹד אַחַת.

cognates.gloss: one; (with a negative) anyone, no one; (of God) the One
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give أَحَدٌ as “one, the first of the numbers”, used absolutely in negative phrases (“not one, no one”), and as an epithet of God, “the One, the Sole … who has no second”, the Arabic use answering to Deu 6:4. Form II أَحَّدَ is “make one; make the two become one”.

evidence.note: “originally وَحَدٌ … One; the first of the numbers … الأَحَدُ, as an epithet, is applied to God alone … and signifies The One; the Sole; He who has ever been one and alone … He who has no second”; it “is used absolutely in negative phrases”.
“He made it one; or called it one … أَحِّدِ الِاثْنَيْنِ Make thou the two to become one.”

cognates.note: The ordinary Arabic “one”, from the root وحد, of which Lane’s sources take أَحَدٌ to be a by-form (و changed to أ). وَحِيدٌ is “a man alone, by himself, apart from others”, as אֶחָד in Ecc 4:8.

evidence.note: “One; the first of the numbers … [and one alone: a single person or thing]”.
“A man alone; by himself; apart from others; solitary; lonely … as also أَحَدٌ”.

cognates.note: Ugaritic keeps ḥ and ḫ apart and writes ḥ here. With the adverbial ending, aḥdh is “at once, together”, the sense of Hebrew כְּאֶחָד.

evidence.note: “aḥd /ʾaḥad-/, fem. aḥt /ʾaḥatt-/ ‘one’ (H. ʾæḥād …; Arab. ʾaḥad)”; “aḥdh with adverbial -h ‘at once, together’ (cf. H. yaḥdāw)”. Read from the OCR text, which garbles the diacritics.

cognates.note: Used in Punic as in Hebrew both for the number, in compounds like “forty-one”, and distributively, “for each”, as אֶחָד in Num 7:11.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ʾeḥḥad, fem. ʾaḥḥat] 1. num. ONE”, KAI 143.4 (NPu) ʾwʾ šʾnt ʾrbʿm wḥd, “She lived forty-one years”; “2. pron. EACH, EACH ONE”, KAI 69.3 (Pu) … lkhnm ksp ʿšrt 10 bʾḥd, “the priests shall receive ten 10 silver for each”.

evidence.locator: Geʿez አሐዱ (ʾäḥädu), num: one (1); አሐቲ (ʾäḥätti), feminine

cognates.note: Akkadian, which lost ḥ, keeps the word not as its ordinary “one” (ištēn, another word) but for “single, alone, sole”: the sense of אֶחָד in Ecc 4:8 and Isa 51:2.

evidence.note: Senses “alone”, “only”, “single”, “solitary”; forms ēdu, wēdum.
“alone; free-standing; lone (person); only; single; sole”.

cognates.gloss: one, single, particular; (כַּחֲדָא) together; (חַד בְּשַׁבָּא) the first day of the week
cognates.note: The Targums render אֶחָד by it from Gen 1:5 on; כַּחֲדָא “together” answers to כְּאֶחָד, and חַד בְּשַׁבָּא is the Peshitta’s “first day of the week”.

evidence.note: “= h. אֶחָד, one, singular, particular. Targ. Gen. I, 5 … חד בשבא first day in the week. Targ. II Esth. III, 7 … כַּחֲדָא [like one,] together, simultaneously. Targ. Ps. II, 2”.

doctrine.statement: Moses tells Israel, “Yahweh, he is God; there is none else beside him” (Deu 4:35, 39), and then, “Hear, O Israel: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one” (Deu 6:4). Malachi asks, “Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us?” (Mal 2:10). Jesus quotes Deu 6:4–5 as the first of all the commandments, and the scribe expounds it, “he is one, and there is none other but he”, which Jesus approves (Mrk 12:29–34). Jesus himself speaks to the Father as “the only true God”, and of himself as the one “you have sent” (Jhn 17:3); Paul writes “to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things … and one Lord Jesus Christ” (1Co 8:6), and “there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus” (1Ti 2:5). Where אֶחָד makes many into one, the text names the parts that are joined (a man and his wife, Gen 2:24; two peoples, Gen 34:16; two sticks, Ezk 37:17); in Deu 6:4 it is said of Yahweh alone, and scripture’s own exposition is “none other but he”. From the verses: the one God of the Shema is the Father; the Son is distinct from him, sent by him, the man who mediates between God and men.

A man “shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh” (Gen 2:24). Jesus answers the question of divorce from this verse: “they are no more two, but one flesh; what therefore God has joined together, let not man separate” (Mat 19:4–6). Malachi asks why God made one, and charges Israel not to deal treacherously with the wife of their youth (Mal 2:14–15); Paul warns that he who is joined to a harlot is one body with her, “for the two, he says, shall be one flesh” (1Co 6:16), and he applies Gen 2:24 to Christ and the ecclesia (Eph 5:31–32). From the verses: marriage makes two into one by God’s own joining, so that to break it is to divide what God has made one; and it is the pattern of Christ and his ecclesia.

Ezekiel is to join the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph “into one stick”; Yahweh will gather the sons of Israel from the nations into their own land and make them “one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king to them all; and they shall no more be two nations”, with “my servant David” as king and “one shepherd” over them (Ezk 37:16–24; 34:23). Jeremiah promises them “one heart and one way” (Jer 32:39). The angel tells Mary that God will give her son “the throne of his father David, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever” (Luk 1:32–33). Jesus says his other sheep too must be brought, “and there shall be one flock, one shepherd” (Jhn 10:16), and prays that those who believe “may be one, as we are one” (Jhn 17:21–22), as he had said “I and the Father are one” (Jhn 10:30). From the verses: the one shepherd of Ezekiel is David’s son, Jesus, who will reign over Israel reunited in its land and gather believers into one flock; and the oneness of the Father and the Son is one that believers are to share, a oneness of heart, will and purpose, not of being.

Under the law the high priest made a covering on the altar of incense and for all Israel’s sins “once in the year” (Exo 30:10; Lev 16:34), year after year. Hebrews sets this beside Christ: the high priest went into the second tabernacle “once every year, not without blood” (Heb 9:7), but Christ, “now once in the end of the ages, has been manifested to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself”, and “was once offered to bear the sins of many” (Heb 9:26, 28). Haggai’s “yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens and the earth” (Hag 2:6) Hebrews expounds as “the removing of those things that are shaken … that the things which cannot be shaken may remain”, so that “we receive a kingdom which cannot be moved” (Heb 12:26–28), while the first covenant was “ready to vanish away” (Heb 8:13). From the verses: the yearly “once” of the law looked to Christ’s one offering, never to be repeated; and the “yet once” of Haggai is the shaking that removed the Mosaic order to leave the kingdom that cannot be shaken.

The Preacher says of the sons of men and the beasts, “one event befalls them: as the one dies, so dies the other; they have all one breath (רוּחַ אֶחָד), and man has no advantage over the beast … all go to one place; all are of the dust, and all return to dust” (Ecc 3:19–20). This is the sentence of Gen 3:19, “dust you are, and to dust you shall return”. From the verses: in death man and beast share one lot and one place; nothing in man survives death of itself, and his hope lies elsewhere than in his own nature.

The first day of creation is counted “there was evening and there was morning, day one (יוֹם אֶחָד)”, and the count runs on, “a second day”, “a third day”, to “the sixth day” (Gen 1:5, 8, 13, 31). The fourth commandment rests on the same count: “in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day” (Exo 20:11). From the verses: each day of creation is one day of an evening and a morning, numbered like the days of Israel’s week, and creation was finished in six of them.

“They have all turned aside, together they have become corrupt; there is none who does good, not even one (אֵין גַּם־אֶחָד)” (Psa 14:3). Paul quotes it, with other psalms, to show that Jews and Gentiles “are all under sin”, so that “all have sinned and come short of the glory of God” and are “justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus” (Rom 3:9–12, 23–24). From the verses: not one man has a righteousness of his own to stand on; righteousness is God’s gift through Christ.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 (אֶחָד, Lev 23:18, 19; בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ, 23:24) and Numbers 10 (בְּאַחַת, Num 10:4). Root key אחד as the corpus keys it. Keys: a.cj.aa (970 tokens) on אֶחָד; xa.ai.ab (15 tokens, Biblical Aramaic חַד/חֲדָה, which also files Hebrew Ezk 33:30) on the Aramaic word. a.cj.ac (6 tokens: Ezk 33:30 and five Daniel tokens already counted under xa.ai.ab) is left unnamed so the Daniel tokens are not counted twice; the Hebrew חַד of Ezk 33:30 therefore has no bdb key. a.cp.ap (אַחַת) and h.ap.af (חַד) are zero-token cross-references to a.cj.aa; xa.ai.aa is a zero-token root key. Left out: a.cj.ab אֵחוּד, the name Ehud of 1Ch 8:6 (belongs in names/, not written in this task); Ezk 21:21 הִתְאַחֲדִי, which the corpus files under חדד (h.aq.aa), “be sharp”; and the root יחד (יַחַד, יַחְדָּו, יָחִיד), which cognates suggest may go back to the same older word (Arabic wāḥid/waḥīd beside ʾaḥad; Ugaritic aḥdh “together” compared with יַחְדָּו), but which the corpus keys as a separate root. Peshitta: the brief’s “Peshitta cognate root” אחד is the Syriac of Hebrew אחז “seize”, not this root; Syriac “one” is SEDRA root 595 חד, lexeme 950 ܚܕ (Greek links εἷς ×324, ἀλλήλων ×74), with 951 ܚܕ ܒܫܒܐ “Sunday”, 952 ܚܕܕܐ “one another”, 953 ܚܕܥܣܪ “eleven” and 954 ܡܚܕܐ “at once, immediately” (εὐθέως ×37), the last three not entered as words; review whether ܡܚܕܐ should be. Peshitta readings checked against the SEDRA word tables in data/haqor.db. Hag 2:6: MACULA aligns ἅπαξ with מְעַט, leaving אַחַת unaligned; the LXX has ἔτι ἅπαξ. Not consulted: Dillmann and Leslau for Geʿez አሐዱ (only Wiktionary and Anderson–Moser cited), DULAT for Ugaritic, CAD for Akkadian wēdu, Biella for Sabaic ʾḥd. Open questions: (1) the doctrine one-god states the Father as the one God of Deu 6:4 and the Son as distinct; (2) once-for-all reads Hag 2:6 / Heb 12:26–28 as the removing of the Mosaic order; (3) one-nation-one-shepherd reads Ezk 37 as Christ’s reign over reunited Israel in the land; (4) Mal 2:15 kept under one-same with a note that its syntax is hard.
